newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers let some foreigners through.
newsitem.headline: French truckers let some foreigners through.

text.p: French truckers let tens of Spanish and Portuguese colleagues slip through their roadblocks around Bordeaux on Friday as anger rose up among foreigners caught up in the five-day-old protest.
Unions said the foreign trucks made their way through a giant trafic jam caused by some 2,000 trucks blocking the road towards Bayonne and the Spanish border.
"We let go those who were the first in line because soke of themn had been away from home for two weeks and we were having logistics problems to feed them," said unonist Christian Laflaquiere.
He said the foreign drivers were very tired and voiced concern for safety on the juggernauts' long road home.
"We advise motorists caution on the Bordeaux-Spain route," he said.
Other truckers preferred to lock up their vehicles and take the train home.

Thousands of foreign trucks, needing to drive through France between northern and southern Europe, are stranded across the country by the protests by French truckers demanding wage hikes, shorter working hours and the right to retire at 55 rather than 60.
The Spanish consulate in Paris has advised its stranded nationals to lodge complaints with local police in order to be able to claim compensation for rotting cargoes.
More than 1,000 British lorry drivers were sleeping in their cabs, running out of food and money, and British freight operators said the dispute was ruining them.

The British Foreign Office warned motorists of considerable traffic disruption, and ordered consulates to help stranded truckers by repatriating them in a medical emergency, relay messages home, advancing cash or helping relatives mail money.
